title: ASU Student Sandarsh Krishna Found Dead at Grand Canyon After 10-Day Search
excerpt: Body of 26-year-old Indian graduate student recovered near South Rim; cause of death remains under investigation
body:
**A Search That Ended in Tragedy**

The National Park Service recovered the body of Sandarsh Krishna, a 26-year-old Arizona State University graduate student from India, near Verkamp's Visitor Center at the Grand Canyon South Rim on May 9 — ending a harrowing 10-day search that gripped the Indian-American community.

Krishna was last seen on April 27 along the Rim Trail during what appeared to be a solo visit to the park. He had reportedly used a rideshare service to reach the Grand Canyon. When he failed to return, authorities launched an extensive search involving aerial surveillance and ground teams combing the rugged terrain below the South Rim.

**No Foul Play Indicated**

Investigators say there is no current indication of foul play, though the cause of death has not been established. Authorities are seeking information about a black backpack Krishna was believed to be carrying at the time of his disappearance.

Krishna was an F-1 visa holder just days away from completing his graduate degree at ASU. His family in India had made public appeals for help during the search. The Indian consulate was in contact with authorities throughout the investigation.

The Grand Canyon averages about 12 deaths per year, many from falls, heat exposure, or drowning.

sources.label: National Park Service via Outside Online

nri_angle: Krishna's death highlights the vulnerability of Indian students navigating life in America far from family — and the anguish of parents thousands of miles away during a crisis.
author: Diaspora Desk
